title: Sleep Duration vs Target Trend
dataSources: Apple Health metrics (`apple:health`), Oura Ring readiness/sleep (`oura:daily`), Whoop recovery/strain (`whoop:cycle`), Withings measurements (`withings:measure`).
app: Apple Health / Apple Watch exports (Health Auto Export or Shortcuts) via HEC; Oura, Whoop, Withings, and Dexcom APIs via scripted REST inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=oura:daily
| eval sleep_h=round(total_sleep_s/3600,1)
| timechart span=1d avg(sleep_h) as hours
| eval target=7.5, deficit=round(target-hours,1)
description: Trends how many hours you actually sleep each night against a personal target so chronic sleep debt becomes visible instead of vague.
value: Sleep debt accumulates invisibly; a daily target comparison turns 'I feel tired' into a number you can act on.
implementation: Ingest Oura or Apple sleep data; schedule daily and review the running deficit against your target.
visualization: Line chart of nightly sleep hours with a target line.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Oura Ring — Oura Cloud API v2 → HEC scripted input.
• **Subcategory context**: Health, Sleep & Wearables — typical feeds: Apple Health metrics (`apple:health`), Oura Ring daily readiness/sleep (`oura:daily`), Whoop recovery/strain (`whoop:cycle`), Withings body/blood-pressure (`withings:measure`), Dexcom CGM glucose (`de.
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `oura:daily`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Oura Ring** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=oura:daily`.

**Collection method:** Oura Cloud API v2 → HEC scripted input.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `GET /v2/usercollection/daily_sleep`.

**Suggested poll interval:** 86400s (daily sync).

**Key fields to extract:** `score, contributors, heart_rate, hrv`.

**Typical connector stack:** Apple Health / Apple Watch exports (Health Auto Export, Shortcuts) via HEC; Oura, Whoop, Withings, Dexcom APIs via scripted REST inputs..

**Author notes:** Ingest Oura or Apple sleep data; schedule daily and review the running deficit against your target.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "oura:daily", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=oura:daily earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Sleep Duration vs Target Trend** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=oura:daily`) across the full search range. The `avg` aggregation groups by the time bucket; change the `by` clause if you want per-device, per-room, or per-user breakdowns instead.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=oura:daily
| eval sleep_h=round(total_sleep_s/3600,1)
| timechart span=1d avg(sleep_h) as hours
| eval target=7.5, deficit=round(target-hours,1)
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Oura app → Readiness / Sleep tabs. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=oura:daily earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, sourcetype, host
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=oura:daily earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.2.2: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Line Chart Of Nightly Sleep Hours With A Target Line (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Oura Ring — no Oura Ring events / missing fields:** If `oura:daily` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Oura Ring connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Oura Ring — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Oura Ring JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=oura:daily | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Oura Ring — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Oura Ring — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Oura Ring APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1d` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1d` buckets.
